hard_gates.evidence: On the clean clone's demo (100,005 alnoor users, 1,005 gulfsteel users) I signed in as admin@alnoor and attacked gulfsteel. attack-api-lists.txt: GET, PUT and DELETE on B's personal and shared view ids through both views/{id} and shared-views/{id} all answered 404, and B's views kept their versions. Searches and filters for gulfsteel returned total 0. B's keyset cursor returned only A's rows. Group sums equalled A's total. The filtered CSV export held no gulfsteel row, and tenant headers got 401 without a session. attack-sweep-get.txt: 523 GET calls covered every GET route in the OpenAPI document. They used B's user, role, company, branch, access and view ids as path ids and as company/role parameters, plus B's search terms, filters and cursor, in JSON and CSV. That found 0 leaks across 217 markers. db-inspect.txt: erp_app is not superuser and has no BYPASSRLS. As erp_app with no tenant set, identity.users and lists.saved_views return 0 rows. lists.saved_views has forced RLS. pg_class estimates and pg_stat_user_tables are refused.

hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches tenant leaks planted in p05's surface
hard_gates.evidence: I planted L14 (L14-list-first-page-kept-in-origin-file-system.patch, 44 lines in p05's web/src/kernel/lists/useListRows.ts). It writes each list query's first page to the origin's private file system (navigator.storage.getDirectory), keyed by endpoint and query only, with no tenant or user. It shows that page right away while the fresh page loads. Every client gate missed it: G1ClientStateTests passed 4 of 4 (run-plants-L13-P13-L14-gates-all.log), the web client-isolation unit tests passed, and the e2e specs/client-isolation.spec.ts passed 5 of 5 against a planted stack (run-L14-e2e-client-isolation.log). Live (plant-live-L14.txt): gulfsteel's admin opens Users and signs out. The signed-out screen's origin file system still holds a 34 KB file with 100 @gulfsteel e-mails. Alnoor's admin then signs in in the same browser. With a 3 s API delay, Users opens on 32 rows, all gulfsteel users, labelled '1,005 users' (10-plant-L14-second-tenant-sees-first-tenants-users.jpg). Regression from round 12: plant L13 is now caught by G1OutsideProcessStateTests, G1TenantSourceTests and, dynamically, G1ListVolumeTests (3 m 35 s).

biggest_gap.title: The client-side tenant gate cannot see the browser's origin private file system, so a list page cached by p05's list component reaches the next tenant on the same device
biggest_gap.detail: p05's list component is the screen every later 100,000-row list uses (Contacts, invoices, stock). Its natural next optimisation is to show the last answer at once while a slow query loads. If it keeps that answer in the origin private file system (navigator.storage.getDirectory), no gate notices. The G1ClientStateTests carrier patterns cover cookies, window.name, history, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, caches, service workers and BroadcastChannel, but not navigator.storage or getDirectory. forgetIdentity() clears storage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage and cookies but never the private file system. The client-isolation e2e judges 12 carriers, and this is not one of them. Its heap snapshot misses the data because the cached rows are replaced and collected once the fresh page arrives. The result is a real cross-tenant leak on shared devices, the outsourced-bookkeeper case the product names. The signed-out device keeps the previous tenant's rows, and the next tenant's list opens on them while the network is slow. Fixes: (a) add navigator.storage, getDirectory, FileSystemHandle, createWritable and storage.persist (and the File System Access API) to the G1ClientStateTests carriers, with a planted self-test; (b) make forgetIdentity empty the origin private file system (getDirectory, then removeEntry with recursive for every entry) and add a Clear-Site-Data: "storage" header to the sign-out answer; (c) add an 'opfs' carrier to client-isolation.spec.ts and its judges' self-test, and have the e2e signed-out step check that the origin's whole storage is empty, using navigator.storage.estimate as well, not a fixed list of APIs.
